analysis:
This batch changes only CI test files for the threat-review scanner; no provider, coordinator or native-runtime code is touched. Because the threat model's assets (A-001..A-017), boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/010/011) and threats are scoped to the provider runtime, no canonical threat applies to these lines.

Changes examined:
(1) .github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py head 186-187 and 196: the integration test now stubs scanner.paid.plan_calls and asserts the planned call counts [2,1]. This is test-only and covers call budgeting.
(2) .github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py head 743: the workflow assertion now requires THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA to come solely from github.event.pull_request.base.sha. The prior env fallback is gone, which tightens pinning of the base context.
(3) Head 752-761: timeout raised to 60 minutes, with THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 3000 and a workload call policy. Defaults are max 500 workload calls and 16384 output tokens, both overridable by repository vars. The tests also assert there is no workflow_dispatch, pr_number or review_depth in the review job. This narrows manual-trigger attack surface under pull_request_target.

The remaining assertions are unchanged: persist-credentials false, no head.sha/head.ref checkout, and hash-pinned pip install.

Integration questions, unverified because the workflow YAML and budget_scan source are not in this batch:
- Whether the actual workflow matches these assertions.
- Whether the raised 60-minute timeout and 500-call default create cost or availability exposure for CI secrets and Bedrock billing. This is a CI concern, not a threat-model asset.
- Whether repository vars can set unbounded values.

These tests cannot regress product security themselves, so no findings are reported.
